newsitem.title: USA: Baltimore Gas net hurt by mild winter.
newsitem.headline: Baltimore Gas net hurt by mild winter.

text.p: Baltimore Gas and Electric Co Friday reported first quarter earnings dropped to $0.43 per share from $0.62 a year earlier, citing the contrast of extremely mild weather conditions to the the colder than normal weather experienced early in 1996.
This weather disparity results in a very unfavorable earnings comparison, the company said.
"The negative impact of the weather was somewhat mitigated by our continued diligence in controlling costs," it added.
Baltimore G&E experienced decreased sales of electricity and natural gas during the first quarter of 1997 compared to the same period last year.

It said total electric sales to customers decreased 6.8 percent. Residential sales decreased 12.6 percent, commercial sales decreased 2.3 percent and industrial sales decreased 1.7 percent, primarily as a result of the weather.

Total natural gas sales to customers for the first three months of 1997 were 5.2 percent below first quarter 1996. This decrease was driven by a 16.1 percent reduction in residential sales as a result of the mild winter weather.
The company said commercial sales increased slightly as customer growth and increased usage offset effects of the weather.

Industrial sales increased 12.7 percent in 1997 due to a significant reduction in interruptions of gas deliveries to customers with alternative fuels when contrasted to the winter of 1996. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
